annotation.title_clean: Executive Summary of the Impact Assessment Report: Proposal for a Directive on adapting non-contractual civil liability rules to artificial intelligence
annotation.title_en: Executive Summary of the Impact Assessment Report: Proposal for a Directive on adapting non-contractual civil liability rules to artificial intelligence
annotation.summary_en: Commission executive summary of the impact assessment for the proposed AI Liability Directive. It identifies fault-based liability gaps caused by AI autonomy and opacity, compares three options, and prefers a staged approach: disclosure and rebuttable presumptions now, with a review after five years of strict liability and mandatory insurance.
key_provisions_or_claims: Fault-based national liability rules are poorly suited to AI because of autonomy and opacity, which make proof of harm costly.
Preferred option 3: ease the burden of proof now (disclosure of evidence, presumption of causality, relief where the AI's inner workings must be shown).
A review clause after five years will reassess harmonised strict liability and mandatory insurance.
Minimum harmonisation is intended to reduce legal uncertainty and fragmentation, especially for SMEs.
Estimated EU-27 AI market value gain of EUR 500m–1.1bn in 2025, and liability insurance premiums up EUR 5.35–16.1m.
